days.title: Western Peaks and High Elevations
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Kreuzjoch
stops.detail: The highest peak is the Kreuzjoch in the southwest at 2558 m above sea level.

stops.name: Hohe Salve
stops.detail: Above this lie weakly metamorphic porphyroids up to 600 m thick (derived from volcanic quartz porphyries and tuffs), mainly in the west (Hohe Salve, Hahnenkamm and Wildseeloder).

days.title: Central Massifs and Geology
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Großen Rettenstein
stops.detail: However, there are also rock formations caused by limestone and dolomite, for example on the Großer Rettenstein.

stops.name: Kitzbüheler Horn
stops.detail: Silurian limestones can also be found in the vicinity of Kitzbühel (e.g. Kitzbüheler Horn), as well as the gray, coarse-grained Schwazer dolomite to the west, which transitions into the Spielberg dolomite to the east as far as Leogang.
